evidence.finding: Actual offered calls rose to 117 versus 79 forecast at 09:15 (+48.1%) and remained materially above forecast in every subsequent interval.
Mean service level declined from 90.85% before the incident to 54.33% during and after it.
Mean ASA increased from 24.78 seconds to 72.50 seconds after incident onset.
Logged-in staffing remained at 49, productive staffing remained at 45–46, and adherence slightly improved.
All four queues experienced broad service-level declines of 26.9–40.2 points alongside offered-volume increases of 48.9%–65.8%, contradicting a localized queue issue.
No visible operational event corroborated a routing or platform incident.

primary_root_cause_detail: Offered demand increased abruptly at 09:15 and remained 24.4%–72.2% above forecast, overwhelming otherwise stable productive capacity across all queues.
recommended_actions: Activate surge staffing or cross-skill support when interval demand materially exceeds forecast.
Apply overflow and callback controls to prevent queue growth during sustained demand surges.
Review the 09:15 demand source and update short-term forecasting and intraday alert thresholds.

rejected_hypotheses.reason: Scheduled and logged-in headcount remained constant, while productive staffing and adherence were stable or slightly improved.
Aggregate AHT was effectively unchanged and queue-level changes were only -0.3% to +0.9%.
The degradation affected every queue, transfer rates remained stable, and no routing event was visible.
No platform event or call-processing disruption was visible; the demand excess directly preceded and explained capacity saturation.
The reported service decline was independently corroborated by higher ASA, near-100% occupancy, and consistent queue-level deterioration.

stakeholder_summary: The service-level incident was most likely caused by an unexpected, sustained demand spike beginning at 09:15. Staffing and AHT remained stable, while all queues experienced higher volume, saturated occupancy, longer waits, and lower service levels.
